domain_label: Turlock Independent Automotive — Business Models & Unit Economics
purpose: A method for reasoning about how each independent automotive-service format in Turlock and Stanislaus County is actually run as a business — its bays and tooling, owner/family and technician-crew labor model, BAR ARD / STAR-smog / DRP licensing gate, cost structure and labeled benchmark margins, supplier chain, and the operating decisions that make a format defensible or doom it — without ever stating a named business's dollar revenue as fact.
assumptions: no observed per-business financials supplied; every dollar band is a labeled industry-benchmark estimate scaled by an observable size signal (bays, trucks, stations, mobile-vs-shop, years in business, DRP language), tagged estimate-not-actual, never a claim of actual revenue for any named business such as Nona's, Balswick's or Complete Collision Works

the universe is the 19 verified independent automotive businesses in Turlock catalogued in businesses.json (national chains, dealer service departments and the informal/mobile tail excluded), in a town of ~72,500 with ~45,000-50,000 registered vehicles and an ag/fleet-heavy, older, higher-mileage parc

city, county, state and demographic figures used here (population, income, ancestry shares, BAR/STAR fees, the $8.25 smog certificate fee) are cited public facts from the deep-dive or labeled derivations, not invented

supplier-to-named-business links (PPG/Axalta/LKQ for collision, ATD/NTW for tires, Transtar for transmission, NAPA/O'Reilly/WORLDPAC and the buying groups for parts) are representative inference about the realistic supply universe, not confirmed contracts, unless a cited source states the relationship
cost-structure and margin benchmarks are published industry figures (gross/labor/parts/net by sub-category) applied as planning priors, not audited operator P&Ls
exclusions: national/franchise chains and new-car dealer service departments (the catalog is independents only) and the informal/mobile backyard tail
stating any actual dollar revenue, profit, or owner income for a specifically named Turlock business as fact
demand-and-saturation market sizing as a standalone deliverable beyond what is needed to judge a format's viability (the sizing detail lives in the market/reconciled analyses)
non-automotive retail and powersports/RV/heavy-truck dealerships except where an auto format straddles into a parts or fleet arm
tax, legal, environmental-permit and labor-law advice for an individual operator; this models formats and decisions, not a specific filing

competency_questions.question: What anchors automotive-service demand in Turlock and which community and parc features make essential mechanical/tire/smog work over-index versus a generic 73k town?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MARKET_PARC_BASE names the resident, household and registered-vehicle figures with cited sources and ties the aging, ag/fleet-heavy, higher-mileage parc to essential-service demand, and COMMUNITY_CHANNELS ties the ~46% Hispanic, Assyrian, Portuguese/Azorean and Punjabi shares to the owner-operated and fleet formats they sustain

competency_questions.question: Why does Turlock sustain roughly 19 cataloged independents and not far more, and how do national chains and Modesto cap that count?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHAIN_MODESTO_LEAKAGE explains the chain crowd-out of commodity lanes and the 15-mile Modesto leakage of high-ticket and specialty work, and SATURATION_WHITESPACE gives the per-sub-category saturation read and where the count is gate-capped versus has headroom

competency_questions.question: How are per-sub-category revenue and margin bands estimated honestly when no per-business revenue is public?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BENCHMARK_REVENUE_METHOD states the published-benchmark-times-observable-size-signal method, the estimate-not-actual label, a confidence level and a confirmation path, and COST_MARGIN_BENCHMARKS supplies the gross/labor/parts/net backbone it scales

competency_questions.question: What licensing must a general repair shop, a smog station, and a collision shop each clear before taking in work?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BAR_ARD_REGISTRATION, SMOG_STAR_LICENSING and DRP_CREDENTIAL_GATE each state the concrete BAR/state/private requirement and fee with its public source, and identify which is the binding entry gate for that format

competency_questions.question: How does owner/family labor let thin-margin formats survive, and where does that lever break?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FAMILY_LABOR_LEVER explains how unpaid/underpaid owner and family labor suppresses the published technician labor-cost benchmark, names the formats most dependent on it (Mando's, E&M, Balswick's, Nona's, solo detailers) and the succession/credential-bottleneck limits

competency_questions.question: What is the realistic supplier universe per sub-category and why do two opposite capital models (JIT service vs inventory-carry parts) coexist?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUPPLY_CHAIN_MAP names the PPG/Axalta/LKQ/Worldpac, NAPA/O'Reilly/WORLDPAC, ATD/NTW, Transtar/NexaMotion and buying-group nodes flagged as representative inference, and CAPEX_LADDER contrasts the JIT service-shop equipment model against the single parts store's shelf-inventory model

competency_questions.question: What does it take to run a general mechanical repair shop, and why is decades-of-trust the moat rather than price?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MECHANICAL_REPAIR_MODEL describes bay/labor operations, the labor-hour revenue engine, the parts-markup line, the benchmark band, and ties the moat to brand trust (Nona's 40+ yrs) and the BAR ARD gate

competency_questions.question: Why is collision the most capital-intensive and gate-dependent format, and how does the thin count of two persist?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COLLISION_BODY_MODEL states the booth/frame capex, the DRP-dependence of volume, the insurer-set rate compression, the benchmark band, and why the count of two is structural not a gap

competency_questions.question: Why is smog the leanest-capex, most defensible recurring-demand format, and what is the honest read on its pricing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SMOG_INSPECTION_MODEL gives the analyzer-as-capital anchor, the test-only vs STAR test-and-repair fork, the $8.25 regulated certificate fee versus the $30-$80 market-price estimate, the recurring DMV-driven demand, and the low-COGS profile, and ranks it among the most defensible segments in SATURATION_WHITESPACE

competency_questions.question: What distinguishes the tire/wheel and transmission models, and where is each one's thin or fragile margin?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TIRES_WHEELS_MODEL names the thin tire-resale margin rescued by service attach (Balswick's, Mando's, Countryside) and TRANSMISSION_MODEL names the high-ARO low-volume specialty with margin in skilled labor (Al's ATRA, Turlock Transmissions) and the EV erosion risk

competency_questions.question: Why is detailing the lowest-barrier, most-crowded independent lane, and how do operators escape the commodity floor?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DETAILING_MODEL identifies the no-BAR-license mobile-capable low capex that drives the highest count (5), the ceramic-coating/paint-correction upsell as the escape from the wash-tier race to the bottom, and the large informal tail

competency_questions.question: Given the parc, cost, licensing and saturation, what is the merged go/no-go on entering or running a given automotive format in Turlock?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FORMAT_GO_NOGO composes saturation, cost/licensing gate and margin reality into a defensible add/avoid verdict (no second independent parts store, no fourth smog without STAR volume, favor fleet/ag specialty, mobile mechanical and EV-readiness) each conditioned on clearing the BAR/STAR/DRP gate

glossary.definition: The binding honesty label on every dollar band in this KB: the figure is a published industry benchmark (revenue per bay / per truck / per station / per car) scaled by an observable Turlock size signal, never a reported or claimed actual revenue for any named business such as Nona's Auto Center or Complete Collision Works.

The vehicle parc — the number, age and mix of cars and light trucks on the road in the Turlock trade area (~45,000-50,000 registered city vehicles plus a rural south-county fleet); auto-service demand keys to the parc, not to households, and Turlock's older ag/fleet-heavy parc over-indexes essential service.

The use of owner and family members as unpaid or below-market labor, which structurally suppresses the published technician labor-cost benchmark and is a main reason owner-operated Turlock shops (Mando's, E&M, Balswick's) clear a profit at single-digit net.

California Bureau of Automotive Repair Automotive Repair Dealer registration, required of any business performing tests, diagnosis or repairs for compensation; it binds nearly every format except pure detailing and is the baseline entry gate under mechanical, collision, tire-repair, smog and transmission work.

A voluntary BAR program letting a licensed smog station inspect DMV-directed vehicles; it carries no application/renewal fee but requires meeting performance standards plus a current ARD and station license, and losing it removes directed-vehicle volume (All Valley and Speed Pass are STAR).

Direct Repair Program — an insurer-shop relationship that routes a large share of collision claims (nationally ~90% of collision revenue) to participating body shops; landing DRP relationships, not finding accident volume, is the real entry wall for a Turlock collision shop.

The survival mechanism in commodity lanes: independents losing the price-shopped product margin (tires, parts) profit instead from attached labor — alignment, brakes, mechanical — so a tire shop lives on service revenue rather than tire-product margin.

An observable proxy (bay count implied by offering, truck/mobile-rig count, station type, years in business, DRP language) used to scale a published per-unit benchmark into a planning revenue band, in place of unavailable actual sales; unit counts are unknown for every named firm.

The single genuinely regulated dollar figure in this sector: California's state-set smog certificate fee per certificate; the widely quoted $30-$80 per-test price is a competitive market band and a labeled estimate, never a regulated fact.

The coverage caveat that the 19-business catalog is a floor not a ceiling — it captures identifiable independents with a web/listing presence and excludes chains, dealers and the informal/mobile tail, so true all-in service density (~6-10 per 10k) far exceeds the cataloged 2.6 per 10k.

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for turlock_auto_models work units in absence of supplied datasets
source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Establish the demand floor every Turlock auto-service format draws on. Unlike food, auto-service demand keys to the vehicle parc, not households: ~72,500 residents (median household income ~$82,995, 2024) in ~23,000-25,000 households at ~1.8-2.0 vehicles/household imply ~45,000-50,000 registered city vehicles (labeled estimate, medium confidence) plus a wider south-county rural trade area. The defining feature is an aging, high-mileage, ag/fleet-heavy parc — dairy, nut and food-processing trucks and trailers driven hard on unimproved roads age faster — which over-indexes the town on essential mechanical, tire, smog and transmission demand versus a generic 73k town. CSU Stanislaus (~9,700 total enrollment) adds a student cohort running older, cash-pay vehicles. This is the size and shape of demand before any format question is asked.

included: resident population, income and household count
the ~45-50k registered-vehicle parc estimate
the aging ag/fleet-heavy parc feature
student older-vehicle demand

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a population, income, vehicle-registration or parc-mix figure is updated

pros.claim: Keying demand to the vehicle parc rather than households grounds every format judgment in the real driver of auto-service volume
pros.example: the ~45-50k-vehicle parc plus an ag/fleet skew explains why essential mechanical and tire demand over-indexes a generic town

cons.claim: A parc estimate built from vehicles-per-household ratios is a derivation, not a registration count, so it carries real width
cons.example: treating ~47k vehicles as precise when the rural-fleet tail and DMV registration data are unmeasured here

failure_modes: treating the resident parc as the independents' addressable volume without subtracting chain and dealer capture
ignoring the ag/fleet skew and modeling a generic suburban parc
acceptance_tests: the demand base cites population, household count and the registered-vehicle parc estimate with its range and confidence, all labeled estimate where derived, and names the ag/fleet-heavy parc feature
revisit_triggers: a Census ACS refresh changes population or income
DMV registration data for the trade area becomes available
the ag/fleet share of the parc shifts

nodes.definition: Tie Turlock's community depth to the auto formats and demand channels it sustains. The town is ~46% Hispanic/Latino (overwhelmingly Mexican-origin), holds a large Assyrian community (~a quarter of the city), a ~7% Portuguese/Azorean share, and a Punjabi/South-Asian presence — each a labor-rich, vehicle-dependent, entrepreneurial base. These communities support more small cash-pay operators than headcount alone implies (enlarging the informal/uncataloged tail), supply Spanish-language and in-language referral channels that lower customer-acquisition cost for owner-operated tire and detailing shops (Mando's), and anchor ag/dairy-fleet and trucking accounts (Portuguese-Azorean dairy ties, Punjabi ag/trucking demand on heavy-mileage fleets). Heritage here drives relationship-based, referral-channel demand rather than ethnic-cuisine-style formats.

included: Hispanic, Assyrian, Portuguese/Azorean and Punjabi shares with sources
in-language referral channels that lower CAC
ag/dairy-fleet and trucking account demand
the enlarged informal/uncataloged tail
excluded: the cost structure of each format

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a community share or the fleet/referral channel it anchors changes

pros.claim: Mapping community channels explains both the owner-operated shop format and the large informal tail the catalog cannot bound
pros.example: Spanish-language referral networks lowering customer-acquisition cost for an owner-operated tire shop like Mando's

cons.claim: Community demand is durable but mostly enlarges the uncataloged tail, so it can be mistaken for cataloged-count headroom
cons.example: reading the large Hispanic base as room for more storefront tire shops when it instead feeds backyard and mobile operators

failure_modes: assuming a large community implies cataloged-count headroom rather than informal-tail growth
overlooking the fleet/trucking accounts the dairy and ag communities anchor
acceptance_tests: each community is given its cited share and the specific channel or fleet demand it anchors, distinguishing cataloged-count effects from informal-tail effects
revisit_triggers: ancestry shares shift in a Census refresh
a community grows or contracts via migration
an ag/dairy or trucking fleet account base changes

nodes.definition: Account for the two biggest caps on the cataloged independent count. First, national chains own the commodity, price-shopped lanes: quick-lube, chain tire (Les Schwab, Big O, Costco, Walmart) and chain parts (AutoZone, O'Reilly, NAPA) plus online (RockAuto, Amazon) absorb the bulk of transactional volume — which is why independent parts retail collapses to a single store and independent tire shops survive only by attaching service. Second, Modesto (15 mi north, ~218k) holds larger collision consolidators, more dealer service and import/specialty shops, so high-ticket collision, warranty and specialty mechanical work leaks north, thinning the Turlock-headquartered count in body and specialty repair. Dealers retain warranty/recall/newer-vehicle work and the informal cash tail pulls the low end away. Any count read that ignores this leakage over-states independent headroom.

included: chain crowd-out of commodity tire/parts/quick-lube lanes
Modesto leakage of high-ticket collision and specialty work
dealer and informal-tail capture
which formats are most exposed
excluded: the measured leakage figure (it is a behavioral estimate, not a count)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: chain footprint, online capture, or Modesto competitive supply shifts

pros.claim: Naming chain crowd-out and Modesto leakage explains why the parc alone over-predicts the independent count
pros.example: chain parts plus online capture is exactly why independent parts retail survives as a single store

cons.claim: The leakage is a behavioral estimate of cross-shopping, not a measured figure, so it can be over- or under-applied
cons.example: assuming all high-ticket collision leaks north when some loyal local DRP volume stays

failure_modes: applying the leakage uniformly to neighborhood-loyal essential formats (smog, owner-op tire) that do not cross-shop
treating the Modesto cap as measured when it is a behavioral estimate
acceptance_tests: the analysis names the chain-dominated commodity lanes and Modesto's size and distance, and ranks formats by exposure to chain and leakage capture, flagging the figure as a behavioral estimate
revisit_triggers: a major collision consolidator or chain footprint opens in Modesto or Turlock
a cross-shop leakage study is produced
a national chain enters or exits a commodity lane locally

nodes.definition: Lay down the published, cited cost-structure backbone every format model is read against. Mechanical repair: gross margin ~50-60% est., labor margin ~50-75% / parts margin ~20-30% est., parts ~30-40% of revenue, net ~6-10% est. (avg ~6.3%), national labor rate ~$120-$159/hr (2026) est. Collision: similar gross but insurer-set DRP rates compress labor, net ~3-8% est. Detailing: gross ~50-70% (solo/mobile 60-80%) est., ceramic-coating ~50% est. Smog: revenue per inspection is market price plus the $8.25 fixed certificate fee, very low COGS. Tires/transmission/parts: thin tire-resale and parts margins offset by service attach and buying-group rebates; transmission high-ticket/low-volume with margin in skilled labor. These are planning priors, not audited P&Ls, and they are the lens that turns a revenue band into a margin reality.

included: gross/labor/parts/net benchmark ranges by sub-category
the $8.25 regulated smog fee versus unregulated test price
the labor-rate range
the planning-prior status of the figures

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a published cost-structure benchmark, labor rate or net-margin figure is revised

pros.claim: Pairing every revenue band with its gross/labor/parts/net benchmark stops high gross from being mistaken for high profit
pros.example: a collision shop benchmarking $1M+ gross still nets only 3-8% because insurer-set DRP rates compress labor

cons.claim: Published benchmarks lag and average away the family-labor and Central-Valley wage-rate differences that move real Turlock margins
cons.example: a national $120-$159/hr labor rate overstates the achievable rate in a sub-coastal Valley market

failure_modes: importing a national benchmark without adjusting for family labor or sub-coastal Valley labor rates
reading a benchmark range as a single point estimate
acceptance_tests: gross, labor, parts and net benchmark ranges are stated by sub-category with sources and labeled planning priors, and the $8.25 regulated fee is distinguished from the unregulated test price
revisit_triggers: a new industry benchmark guide is published
labor-rate or parts-cost inflation shifts the cost shares
a net-margin base-rate update lands

nodes.definition: Define the only honest way to attach a revenue band to a format when no per-business revenue is public: take a published per-unit benchmark (~$203k revenue/bay PartsTech 2025; independent tire store $500k-$2M; profitable smog station $180k-$450k/yr; ~$1.2M average collision shop; transmission $250k-$500k/bay; ~$250k average detailing establishment; independent parts store $500k-$2M) and scale it by an observable Turlock size signal (bay count implied by offering, mobile-vs-shop, station type, DRP language, years in business), then tag the result estimate-not-actual, assign a confidence, and name the confirmation path (CDTFA seller's-permit receipts, BAR station data, or POS bay-hours x labor rate). Unit counts (bays, trucks, stations) are unknown for every named firm, so bands are wide on purpose, and Central Valley labor rates sit modestly below coastal CA so true figures likely land at the lower-middle of each band. The seven sub-categories span a ~30x per-firm revenue range, so there is no typical auto business and a naive total-divided-by-19 is meaningless.

included: benchmark-times-size-signal method
the estimate-not-actual label, confidence and confirmation path
the ~30x per-firm range and the no-typical-business point
excluded: stating a named business's actual revenue

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a benchmark, a size signal, or the availability of confirming sales-tax/BAR data changes

pros.claim: A labeled benchmark band gives a defensible planning number without ever claiming a private business's actual revenue
pros.example: a 3-4 bay shop at ~$203k/bay scales to a band tagged estimate with a seller's-permit confirmation path

cons.claim: A benchmark band can be over-trusted if the unknown unit count is mis-inferred or the confidence label is dropped
cons.example: treating an inferred bay count as precise when the shop's true bay and throughput are unknown

failure_modes: dropping the estimate-not-actual label and presenting a band as a fact
dividing a sector total by 19 and reporting it as a typical business across a 30x range
acceptance_tests: every revenue band produced carries the estimate-not-actual label, a confidence level, the size signal used, and a named confirmation source, and the ~30x per-firm range is stated so no typical business is implied
revisit_triggers: a published per-bay/per-station/per-shop benchmark is updated
CDTFA or BAR station data becomes available
a format's observable size signal changes

nodes.definition: Explain the swing variable that lets Turlock's thin-margin independents survive: owner and family labor, paid below market or not at all, structurally suppresses the published technician labor-cost benchmark and is a main reason owner-operated formats clear a profit on 6-10% net. The catalog is family-run heavy — Broadway (family-owned), E&M (family-owned since 2012), Nona's (40+ yrs), Mando's (family-owned), Balswick's (since 1945). The formats most dependent on it are owner-op tire/wheel, general mechanical, and solo/mobile detailing. The lever has hard limits: it caps growth at the family's capacity, masks the true cost of labor when planning a sale, and — distinct from food — it cannot substitute for credential-gated labor (a licensed smog inspector or I-CAR/ASE DRP technician), so the credential bottleneck, not family willingness, caps the gated formats.

included: how family labor suppresses the technician labor benchmark
which formats most depend on it
the succession/burnout/scaling limits
the credential-bottleneck limit that family labor cannot clear

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a family-labor dependency, succession event, or licensed-technician supply change occurs

pros.claim: Naming family labor as the survival lever explains how owner-op shops run on margins that would sink a fully-staffed operator
pros.example: Mando's owner-operated tire/wheel model absorbing labor in-family to clear value-priced work

cons.claim: Family labor is invisible on a benchmark P&L and cannot clear a credential gate, so it both understates true cost and fails where licensed labor is required
cons.example: a buyer who must hire out the owner's unpaid hours, or a smog station that still needs a licensed inspector regardless of family willingness

failure_modes: modeling a format at benchmark labor cost and missing that its survival is unpaid family hours
assuming family labor can clear a credential-gated role like a licensed smog inspector
acceptance_tests: the analysis states how family labor moves the labor share, names the most dependent formats, and flags both the succession/burnout limit and the credential-bottleneck it cannot clear
revisit_triggers: an operator approaches succession or sale
family capacity changes (illness, departure, growth past it)
a licensed-technician shortage or wage change alters the hired-labor alternative

nodes.definition: Map the realistic supply universe each sub-category draws on, flagged as representative inference rather than confirmed contracts. Collision (Broadway, Complete Collision Works): paint PPG/Axalta via PBE jobbers/LKQ Refinish, parts OE dealer plus LKQ aftermarket/recycled and Worldpac OE. Mechanical (Nona's, Turlock Auto Service, E&M): NAPA/O'Reilly/WORLDPAC jobbers plus local Turlock Auto Parts, OE dealer for special-order, possible Alliance/Federated-Pronto program access. Tires (Balswick's, Countryside, Mando's): American Tire Distributors and NTW plus direct Michelin/Goodyear. Transmission (Al's, Turlock Transmissions): Transtar/NexaMotion soft-parts and master kits, torque converters, recycled units via Transend. Parts retail (Turlock Auto Parts): warehouse distributors plus buying groups (Aftermarket Auto Parts Alliance, Federated, National Pronto). Supplier-to-named-business links are inference unless a cited source states the relationship; named distributors are the verified-to-serve-this-geography universe.

the inference label on supplier-to-business links
the verified-to-serve-this-geography universe

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a supplier relationship, buying-group membership, or documented link changes

pros.claim: A sub-category-to-supplier map shows the realistic, verified-to-serve-this-geography supply universe behind each model
pros.example: collision drawing on PPG/Axalta paint and LKQ aftermarket panels fitting next-day job-by-job ordering

nodes.definition: Map the capital-intensity ladder that gates format entry independent of demand, and the two opposite capital models that coexist. The ladder low-to-high: mobile detailing rig ($5k-$15k est.) -> fixed detailing / per-bay mechanical tooling (mid-five-figures to $50k-$150k est.) -> the smog analyzer (concentrated single-instrument capex plus BAR connectivity) -> collision booth + frame ($50k-$150k+ est.), the heaviest in the sector. The deeper structural split is between the JIT service shops (mechanical, collision, transmission, tires) that tie up capital in equipment and labor and order parts per job, and the single parts retailer that ties up capital in shelf inventory and broad SKU depth. This is the structural reason a town this size supports many service shops but only one independent parts store: the inventory-carry model needs scale the local independent channel cannot give it against the nationals. Two formats can face the same parc demand but very different up-front and working capital.

included: the low-to-high capex ladder per format
the JIT-service vs inventory-carry capital split
capex as a demand-independent entry gate

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: equipment cost, financing, or the parts-channel scale changes

pros.claim: Surfacing the capex ladder and the two capital models shows why a demand-true lane may still be hard to enter
pros.example: collision booth + frame capex gating a format whose accident demand is not the obstacle

cons.claim: Capex figures vary widely by new-vs-used and scale, so this is a relative-intensity ranking not a quote
cons.example: a used analyzer or lift dropping a shop's entry cost well below a new build-out

failure_modes: judging a lane on demand alone and ignoring its capital anchor
treating the inventory-carry parts model as comparable to a JIT service shop's capital needs
acceptance_tests: the capex ladder is ranked low-to-high with labeled estimates and the JIT-service vs inventory-carry split is named as the reason for the single parts store
revisit_triggers: equipment prices or financing terms change
a used-equipment opportunity changes a format's entry cost
a parts-channel scale shift changes the inventory model

nodes.definition: Establish the baseline licensing nearly every format must clear: a California Bureau of Automotive Repair Automotive Repair Dealer (ARD) registration is required of any business performing tests, diagnosis or repairs for compensation, plus a City of Turlock business license, a CDTFA seller's permit for any shop reselling parts/tires, and local/air-district and hazmat compliance (used oil, solvents, ATF, tires). This binds mechanical, collision, tire-when-doing-repair, smog and transmission — essentially every format except pure detailing, which clears no BAR gate. The ARD floor is cheaper and faster than the STAR or DRP gates but mandatory, and it is the reason detailing is the lowest-barrier, highest-count lane while every repair format starts from a registration and compliance baseline.

included: BAR ARD registration and renewal
city business license and CDTFA seller's permit
hazmat/air-district compliance
the no-BAR-gate detailing exception

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a BAR ARD, city license, seller's-permit or hazmat requirement or fee changes

pros.claim: Treating the BAR ARD as the mandatory floor prevents a model that ignores registration and hazmat compliance
pros.example: a repair concept budgeting ARD registration, seller's permit and used-oil/solvent disposal before opening

cons.claim: The ARD floor is modest, so it can lull an operator into underestimating the costlier STAR and DRP gates
cons.example: assuming a cheap ARD registration means easy entry for a smog or collision concept

failure_modes: skipping the seller's permit or hazmat compliance and facing penalties after opening
confusing the cheap ARD floor with the costlier STAR or DRP gates
acceptance_tests: the BAR ARD registration, the city business license, the CDTFA seller's permit and hazmat compliance are stated with public sources as the mandatory repair-format floor, and detailing's no-BAR exception is named
revisit_triggers: BAR or city fee schedules change
an air-district or hazmat requirement changes
a format changes its services enough to require ARD scope changes

nodes.definition: Define the smog-specific licensing fork that caps the smog count to a handful of properly licensed stations. A smog station is licensed test-and-repair, test-only, or repair-only; inspectors hold a separate BAR license (~$20 application / ~$20 renewal per 2 years), the state-set certificate fee is $8.25 per certificate, and crucially the inspection price itself is NOT regulated by BAR. STAR certification is voluntary, carries no application/renewal fee, and lets a station inspect DMV-directed vehicles, but it requires meeting performance standards plus a current ARD and station license; losing STAR removes directed-vehicle volume. All Valley Smog and Speed Pass Smog are STAR (test-and-repair vs test-only); Turlock Quick Smog & Repair adds repair. The licensed-inspector requirement is a credential bottleneck, not a willingness one, which is the binding gate alongside the analyzer capex.

included: station license types and the technician-license requirement
the $8.25 regulated certificate fee and the unregulated inspection price
STAR certification and its directed-vehicle volume
the inspector credential bottleneck

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a STAR rule, smog fee, or licensed-inspector supply changes

pros.claim: Distinguishing the $8.25 regulated fee from the unregulated test price and STAR from the base station license shows the true smog entry gate
pros.example: a test-only station like Speed Pass clearing the leanest capex but still needing a licensed inspector and STAR for directed volume

cons.claim: STAR performance standards and directed-volume value shift with program rules, so the gate is a moving target not a fixed fee
cons.example: a station losing STAR on a performance metric and with it the directed-vehicle volume

failure_modes: presenting the $30-$80 test price as a regulated fact rather than the $8.25 certificate fee
budgeting the analyzer but not the licensed-inspector credential bottleneck
acceptance_tests: the station-license types, the licensed-inspector requirement, the $8.25 regulated fee versus the unregulated price, and the STAR directed-vehicle role are stated with sources, and the credential bottleneck is named as the binding gate
revisit_triggers: BAR/STAR program rules or fees change
the directed-vehicle volume value moves
a licensed-inspector shortage develops

nodes.definition: Establish the binding entry gate for the collision format. Body shops need a BAR ARD, but the structural barrier is twofold: I-CAR Gold Class / ASE certification are de-facto required for DRP work (private credentials, not state licenses) plus air-district paint-booth VOC permits and hazmat handling; and the volume itself is DRP-dependent — nationally ~90% of collision revenue flows via DRP claims and ~82% of insured drivers use a DRP shop. A new body shop's real obstacle is landing insurer DRP relationships and financing $50k-$150k+ of booth/frame capex, not finding accident volume. This is the structural reason the local collision count is just two (Broadway, Complete Collision Works): the thin count is the gate, not a market gap. Whether either named shop holds specific DRP contracts is unknown; DRP is confirmed as the volume driver, the specific contracts are not.

included: I-CAR/ASE and air-district booth credentials
DRP-dependence of collision volume
the booth/frame capex tie
the count-is-the-gate read
excluded: the collision operating model's cost detail (that is its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a DRP program, certification standard, or booth-permit rule changes

pros.claim: Identifying DRP relationships and certification as the binding gate corrects the assumption that accident volume is the collision obstacle
pros.example: a new body shop blocked not by demand but by an inability to land insurer DRP relationships

cons.claim: Whether a specific named shop holds a DRP contract is unknown, so the gate is a structural fact whose firm-level application is inference
cons.example: asserting Complete Collision Works holds a particular insurer DRP without a cited source

failure_modes: budgeting only the ARD and booth and missing that DRP relationships gate the volume
treating the thin count of two as a market gap rather than a structural gate
acceptance_tests: the I-CAR/ASE and booth-permit credentials, the DRP-dependence of volume, and the booth/frame capex are stated with sources, and the count-of-two is explained as the gate not a gap
revisit_triggers: a DRP program or certification standard changes
an air-district booth-permit rule changes
a documented firm-level DRP contract surfaces

nodes.definition: Model the general mechanical repair shop (Nona's Auto Center 40+ yrs, Turlock Auto Service certified one-stop, E&M Auto Service and Parts family-owned since 2012 with A/C, brakes, tires and parts). The revenue engine is billed labor (labor rate x billed hours, with technician billed-vs-paid productivity the lever); parts carry a ~20-30% markup at ~30-40% of revenue. It runs gross ~50-60% and net ~6-10% est. against a national ~$120-$159/hr labor rate (lower in the Valley). Counter operations are JIT — multiple same-day jobber deliveries, minimal shelf stock. It benchmarks ~$203k/bay scaled by inferred bays: small 3-4 bay ~$500k-$900k, established multi-bay ~$900k-$1.8M (estimate-not-actual, medium confidence). The moat is decades of brand trust (Nona's) plus the BAR ARD gate; A/C emphasis (E&M) implies a summer daypart spike in Central Valley heat. Essential, cash-pay and demand-resilient, this is the backbone of the catalog.

included: mechanical bay/labor operations and service offering
labor-hour revenue engine and parts markup
the benchmark band and the trust moat
the A/C summer daypart

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: mechanical labor rate, parts cost, or the generalist count changes

pros.claim: The model shows why decades-of-trust, not price, is the defensible moat in an essential cash-pay lane
pros.example: Nona's 40+ years of brand equity carrying repeat demand a new generalist cannot quickly win

cons.claim: Technician billed-vs-paid productivity and the labor rate cap the model, so volume and rate discipline carry it not parts margin
cons.example: a shop with idle bays losing the labor-hour revenue that the fixed overhead requires

failure_modes: opening an undifferentiated generalist against established trust brands
modeling on parts margin when billed labor hours are the revenue engine
acceptance_tests: the model states the billed-labor revenue engine, the parts-markup line, the estimate-not-actual per-bay band, and ties the moat to brand trust and the BAR ARD gate
revisit_triggers: labor-rate or parts-cost inflation shifts
a new generalist or chain enters the lane
a trust-brand shop changes hands or closes

nodes.definition: Model the tire/wheel shop (Balswick's Tire & Auto Service & Detail since 1945 — the most diversified straddle in the catalog; Countryside Tire & Brake, Balswick's-affiliated; Mando's Tires and Wheels, owner-operated and referral-driven). The defining economics: tire resale margin is thin because national chains (Les Schwab, Big O, Costco, Walmart) and online (Tire Rack, SimpleTire ship-to-installer) absorb commodity tire volume, so independents profit from service attach — mounting/balancing plus alignment, brakes and general mechanical. Capex is moderate (mounting/balancing machines, alignment rack, road-force balancer). It benchmarks single-location owner-op ~$400k-$900k and established tire+service ~$1M-$2.5M (estimate-not-actual, medium). The survival rule is mini-integration: tire + alignment + brake + mechanical wins where standalone tire resale loses, and the Hispanic owner-op channel (Mando's) plus ag/fleet accounts carry referral-driven demand.

included: tire/wheel operations and the thin tire-resale margin
service attach as the profit source
the benchmark band and the owner-op/ag-fleet channel

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: tire-channel competition, service mix, or a fleet account changes

pros.claim: The model shows why independents live on attached service, not tire-product margin, against chain and online tire
pros.example: Balswick's straddling tires + repair + detail so service revenue carries the thin tire line

cons.claim: Thin tire margin and chain/online price competition mean a standalone tire shop without service attach is a structural loser

revisit_triggers: a chain or online tire footprint shifts

a fleet account is won or lost

nodes.definition: Model the smog/inspection station (Speed Pass Smog test-only — the leanest capex in the sector; All Valley Smog STAR test-and-repair; Turlock Quick Smog & Repair, smog + repair capturing fail-then-repair revenue). Revenue per inspection is the unregulated market price (a $30-$80 band, labeled estimate, never a regulated fact) plus the $8.25 fixed certificate fee; COGS is very low and capital is concentrated in the BAR-approved analyzer and connectivity. It benchmarks test-only ~$150k-$300k and STAR test-and-repair (with repair revenue) ~$300k-$600k+ (estimate-not-actual, medium). Demand is steady, recurring and DMV-renewal-driven — the most defensible segment — but price is competitively capped and the volume ceiling is the eligible-vehicle count. The EV transition is the erosion risk: BEVs are smog-exempt, so a slowly electrifying parc directly thins this lane over time.

the $8.25 fee plus unregulated price revenue line
the analyzer capex anchor and recurring DMV demand
the EV-exemption erosion risk
excluded: the licensing fork itself (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a STAR rule, smog price, BEV share, or station count changes

pros.claim: The model identifies the most defensible recurring-demand segment while keeping the pricing honest
pros.example: a test-only station running very low COGS on steady DMV-renewal demand with only the analyzer as capital

cons.claim: Competitive price capping and BEV exemption bound both the price and the long-run volume
cons.example: a station's revenue capped by competitive test pricing and slowly eroded as BEVs exempt from smog grow

ignoring the BEV-exemption erosion of the eligible-vehicle ceiling

revisit_triggers: a STAR rule or fee changes

nodes.definition: Model the auto body/collision shop (Broadway Auto & AutoBody Repair, family-owned collision + dent repair with secondary mechanical; Complete Collision Works, 35+ years with PDR and computerized paint matching consistent with an on-site PPG/Axalta mixing bank). It is the most capital-intensive format: spray booth, frame/measuring system, mixing bank, welders and PDR tools, with booth + frame commonly $50k-$150k+ (estimate, low confidence/wide). Gross is similar to mechanical but insurer-set DRP rates compress labor, so net runs ~3-8% est. Volume is DRP-dependent and the average repair exceeds $4,600 (2024). It benchmarks limited-DRP ~$700k-$1.5M and strong-DRP (Complete Collision 35+) ~$1.5M-$3.5M (estimate-not-actual, medium). The moat is insurer relationships plus certified equipment and longevity; the thin count of two is structural (the DRP/capex gate), and complex high-ticket jobs leak to Modesto consolidators.

included: collision booth/frame capex
DRP-dependent volume and insurer rate compression
the benchmark band and the structural count-of-two
Modesto leakage of complex jobs
excluded: the DRP gate detail itself (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a DRP rate, repair-cost, or Modesto-consolidator shift

pros.claim: The model pairs the high revenue band with the thin DRP-compressed net and the structural gate so high gross is not read as easy profit
pros.example: a strong-DRP shop benchmarking multi-million gross yet netting only 3-8% on insurer-set rates

cons.claim: The top-end band assumes strong DRP and longevity that a new shop cannot quickly win, so the range is wide and gate-conditioned
cons.example: reading Complete Collision's 35-year strong-DRP band as a typical new-entrant outcome

acceptance_tests: the model states the booth/frame capex, the DRP-dependent volume and rate compression, the estimate-not-actual band, and the structural count-of-two read
revisit_triggers: a DRP rate or program changes

nodes.definition: Model the transmission specialty (Al's Transmissions Inc. automatic rebuilds, ATRA-affiliated signaling trade-standard rebuild practice and a warranty network; Turlock Transmissions adding engine, differential, electric and general repair — broad drivetrain). The economics are high average-repair-order ($1,500-$4,000 ARO), low-volume and specialty: margin lives in skilled drivetrain labor, and inputs are Transtar/NexaMotion rebuild kits, torque converters and valve bodies shipped 1-3 days per teardown (JIT), with some common kits stocked. Niche tooling (transmission jacks, dyno/flush, cleaning tank, lifts) is moderate capex. It benchmarks specialty 3-6 bay ~$500k-$1.5M (estimate-not-actual, low-medium) against a $250k-$500k/bay benchmark. Thin by nature and defensible on expertise, but the demand pool shrinks slowly as transmissions get more reliable and EVs (no multi-speed transmission) creep in — making EV erosion the key long-run risk alongside smog.

included: transmission specialty operations and high-ARO low-volume economics
Transtar kit supply and niche tooling capex
the benchmark band and the EV erosion risk
excluded: the supply map detail itself (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a kit cost, BEV share, or reliability trend changes

pros.claim: The model shows a defensible high-ARO specialty whose margin lives in skilled labor, not volume
pros.example: Al's ATRA-affiliated rebuild practice commanding specialty ARO a generalist cannot

cons.claim: Reliability gains and EV adoption slowly shrink the demand pool, so the format faces a structural long-run headwind
cons.example: a BEV having no multi-speed transmission, removing the format's core job over time

failure_modes: modeling the specialty on volume when it is high-ARO low-volume
ignoring the EV/reliability erosion of the demand pool

revisit_triggers: a Transtar/kit cost or availability shift
the BEV share of the parc grows
a transmission-reliability trend changes the demand pool

nodes.definition: Model auto detailing — the lowest-barrier, highest-count independent lane (2 Guys Auto Detailing shop + mobile with ceramic coatings and headlight restoration; Turlock Auto Detailing Co. mobile ceramic/interior/exterior; plus Adrian's, Cen-Cal and Veras as solo/mobile profiles). It clears no BAR license, is mobile-capable, buys chemicals/coatings by the drum from detailing-supply wholesalers, and runs a mobile rig at $5k-$15k or a fixed shop at $50k-$150k. Gross is high (50-70%, solo/mobile 60-80%; ceramic ~50%) but the wash/basic tier is a price-competitive race to the bottom against a large informal tail. It benchmarks solo/mobile ~$60k-$180k and shop+mobile with ceramic ~$120k-$350k (estimate-not-actual, low-medium). The escape from the commodity floor is ceramic coating, paint correction, fleet accounts or detailing-for-dealers; discretionary and weather-sensitive demand skews to dry/warm months and pre-sale prep.

included: no-BAR-license mobile-capable low-capex operations
the wash-tier commodity floor and the large informal tail
ceramic/paint-correction/fleet escape from the floor
weather seasonality and the band

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a ceramic/chemical cost, fleet account, or informal-tail competition changes

pros.claim: The model explains why no-BAR-license low capex drives the highest count and where operators escape the commodity floor
pros.example: 2 Guys upselling ceramic coatings above the commodity wash tier to capture high-margin work

cons.claim: The low barrier means a price-competitive race to the bottom and a large informal tail the catalog cannot bound

revisit_triggers: a ceramic-coating or chemical cost shift

nodes.definition: Model the single independent parts store (Turlock Auto Parts, ASE parts specialists implying a counter-pro labor model serving DIY plus wholesale trade accounts). Uniquely in this sector it is inventory-heavy with broad SKU depth on the shelf — the opposite capital model from the JIT repair shops — with capital tied up in inventory and POS/catalog systems rather than equipment. Margins are thin, offset by buying-group rebates (Aftermarket Auto Parts Alliance, Federated, National Pronto) and daily/weekly warehouse-distributor replenishment with same-day hot-shot to shop accounts. It benchmarks ~$500k-$1.5M (estimate-not-actual, low-medium). It survives not on retail price against AutoZone/O'Reilly/NAPA and online (RockAuto/Amazon) but on ASE counter expertise and trade accounts to local shops — which is precisely why the lane supports only one independent: an inventory-carry model against the nationals is a structural loser without a wholesale/trade base.

included: inventory-carry counter-pro model and trade accounts
buying-group rebate offset and WD replenishment
the benchmark band and the single-survivor structural read
excluded: the repair shops' parts-markup line (covered under mechanical)
the capex split detail itself (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a buying-group rebate, national/online footprint, or trade-account base changes

pros.claim: The model explains the single-survivor outcome through the inventory-carry-vs-JIT capital split and the trade-account base
pros.example: Turlock Auto Parts surviving on ASE counter expertise and shop trade accounts rather than retail price

cons.claim: Thin margins and national/online price competition make the inventory-carry model fragile without scale
cons.example: an independent parts store losing DIY retail to AutoZone and RockAuto online

failure_modes: opening a second independent parts store into a lane the nationals own
running an inventory-carry model without a wholesale/trade-account base
acceptance_tests: the model states the inventory-carry counter-pro model, the buying-group rebate offset, the trade-account survival base, the estimate-not-actual band, and the single-survivor read
revisit_triggers: a buying-group membership or rebate changes
a national or online parts footprint shifts
a wholesale trade-account base changes

nodes.definition: Define the survival mechanism that runs across the commodity lanes: service attach and mini-integration. Standalone tire resale and standalone parts retail lose to chains and online on product margin, so the independents that survive bundle higher-margin labor onto the commodity transaction — tire + alignment + brake + mechanical, smog + repair, detailing + ceramic upsell — and several mini-integrate across categories (E&M sells mechanical + tires + parts; Balswick's does tires + repair + detail; Turlock Quick Smog & Repair bundles smog + repair). This is the cross-cutting lever the format models lean on: it is why functional mechanical-repair capacity materially exceeds the headline count of three primary mechanical shops, and why a new entrant in a commodity lane must attach service rather than compete on product price.

included: service attach as the commodity-lane survival mechanism
cross-category mini-integration examples
why functional mechanical capacity exceeds the headline count
excluded: each format's full unit economics (their own nodes)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a service-attach mix or cross-category straddle changes

pros.claim: Naming service attach as the cross-cutting lever explains both survival in commodity lanes and the under-counted functional capacity
pros.example: E&M mini-integrating mechanical + tires + parts so attached service carries the thin product lines

cons.claim: Service attach depends on the labor and credential base, so a pure-resale operator without it cannot simply bolt it on
cons.example: a tire-only shop unable to add alignment/brake revenue without the bays, tooling and licensed labor

failure_modes: counting only primary categories and understating functional mechanical capacity
assuming a resale-only operator can attach service without the labor and tooling base
acceptance_tests: the lever states service attach as the commodity-lane survival mechanism, names the mini-integration examples, and explains the under-counted functional capacity
revisit_triggers: a shop adds or drops an attached-service line
a commodity-lane margin shifts
a cross-category straddle changes

nodes.definition: Encode the binding honesty charter as a first-class node so it travels with every number and claim in the KB. Per-business dollar revenue is NOT public for these privately held independents, so no dollar figure is ever stated as an actual reported figure for any named business (Nona's, Balswick's, Complete Collision Works, etc.); every revenue, margin and market-size figure is a labeled benchmark estimate carrying the word estimate, a method, a public source basis and a confidence band. Structural facts (suppliers serving the geography, BAR/STAR licensing regimes, state-set fees, demographics) are cited fact; gaps are flagged unknown. Supplier-to-named-business links are representative inference, not confirmed contracts, unless a cited source states the relationship. The one regulated dollar figure is the $8.25 smog certificate fee; the $30-$80 test price is a market estimate. Coverage of 19 is a floor, not a ceiling. This charter dominates any output: method plus public source plus confidence must accompany every number, and an actual-revenue claim for a named business is refused.

included: the no-actual-revenue rule for named businesses
the method+source+confidence requirement on every number
the fact/inference/unknown labeling and the $8.25-vs-market-price and floor-not-ceiling rules
excluded: the specific revenue-band arithmetic (that is the method node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a public financial source, a regulated fee, or a labeling rule changes

pros.claim: Making the honesty charter a node forces method, source and confidence to travel with every figure rather than being assumed
pros.example: a collision band always emitted as estimate-not-actual with a benchmark source and confidence, never as a named shop's real sales

cons.claim: A standing charter can be treated as boilerplate and skimmed unless each number is checked against it
cons.example: a number quoted without its method/source slipping through because the charter was assumed rather than applied

failure_modes: stating a named business's actual revenue as fact
dropping the method/source/confidence that must accompany every number
acceptance_tests: every dollar figure in any output carries the estimate-not-actual label with a method, a public source and a confidence, the $8.25 fee is the only regulated dollar fact, and supplier-to-business links are labeled inference
revisit_triggers: a public per-business financial source appears
a regulated fee or labeling rule changes
a documented supplier contract surfaces that upgrades an inference to fact

nodes.definition: Synthesize the per-sub-category saturation read that explains why ~19 cataloged independents is the equilibrium and where headroom remains. The cataloged-independent density is ~2.6 per 10k (19/72,500x10,000), a FLOOR; true all-in density counting chains, dealers and the informal tail is plausibly ~6-10/10k. Crowded/commoditized (do not add on demand alone): detailing (5, low-barrier race to the bottom, large informal tail) and tires/wheels (3, functionally crowded by chains, survive on service attach). Adequately served: mechanical (3 + cross-sellers, essential cash-pay) and smog (3, recurring defensible but volume-capped). Thin/concentrated by gate (count is the gate, not a gap): collision (2, DRP/capex-gated), transmission (2, specialty), parts retail (1, national-owned lane). Genuine white space, ranked: fleet/ag-vehicle specialty (heavy-mileage diesel tied to the dairy/nut belt), mobile mechanical (extending the detailing low-capex come-to-customer playbook), and EV-readiness (high-voltage service, heavier-EV tires/brakes, near-unserved locally). The count is a capped parc minus chain/Modesto/dealer leakage, partitioned by regulatory and supply-chain gates.

included: the ~2.6/10k floor vs ~6-10/10k all-in density
per-sub-category crowded/adequate/thin reads
the ranked white-space list
the forces behind ~19
excluded: the cost-gate verdict (that is the go/no-go node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a sub-category count, leakage measurement, or parc figure changes

pros.claim: The synthesis turns the parc, leakage and gate forces into an actionable per-sub-category saturation map
pros.example: ranking fleet/ag specialty as genuine white space while flagging a second parts store as a national-owned no-go

cons.claim: Saturation reads are medium confidence absent a measured cross-shop leakage study and unknown unit counts
cons.example: a white-space call a real Modesto-leakage measurement could revise

acceptance_tests: each sub-category gets a crowded/adequate/thin read, the white space is ranked, the floor-vs-all-in density is stated, and the forces behind ~19 are named
revisit_triggers: a cross-shop leakage study lands

nodes.definition: Compose the merged go/no-go verdict on adding or running a given automotive format, the synthesis the whole KB builds toward. It intersects three lenses: demand headroom (SATURATION_WHITESPACE), the cost/licensing gate (BAR_ARD_REGISTRATION, SMOG_STAR_LICENSING, DRP_CREDENTIAL_GATE, CAPEX_LADDER), and the margin reality (COST_MARGIN_BENCHMARKS, FAMILY_LABOR_LEVER, SERVICE_ATTACH_LEVER). The reconciled rule: do not add a second independent parts store (national-owned lane), a fourth smog station without STAR directed-vehicle volume, or a third collision shop against the DRP/capex gate; the defensible headroom is fleet/ag-vehicle specialty, mobile mechanical, and EV-readiness — each viable only after clearing the BAR ARD (and, where relevant, STAR or DRP) gate and, in commodity lanes, attaching service rather than competing on product price. A white space that is demand-true but gate-blocked or unable to attach service is a no-go until the gate is cleared.

included: the three-lens go/no-go intersection
the named add/avoid verdicts
the gate-and-service-attach condition on every white space
excluded: the underlying saturation or licensing detail (their own nodes)

cons.claim: A single verdict can over-simplify a format whose demand, gate and margin point in different directions
cons.example: a fleet/ag specialty with real demand but a credential and tooling barrier needing nuance beyond go/no-go

acceptance_tests: the verdict for a format states the saturation read, the binding licensing/capex gate, the margin reality, and an add/avoid call conditioned on clearing the BAR/STAR/DRP gate and attaching service in commodity lanes
revisit_triggers: a saturation read changes

conflict_axes.name: demand_headroom_vs_licensing_gate
conflict_axes.description: A sub-category with real demand headroom may still be gate-blocked by BAR ARD, STAR or DRP and capex, so demand-true is not the same as enterable.
poles: enter only where the licensing gate clears
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat a demand-true but gate-blocked white space as a no-go until the binding BAR/STAR/DRP gate is cleared

conflict_axes.name: high_gross_vs_thin_net
conflict_axes.description: High-revenue formats (collision, mechanical, transmission) can post strong gross while netting only single digits, so revenue must never be read as profit.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always pair the revenue band with its gross/labor/parts/net benchmark before judging attractiveness

conflict_axes.name: family_labor_survival_vs_credential_bottleneck
conflict_axes.description: Owner/family labor lets a thin-margin format survive but cannot clear a credential gate (licensed smog inspector, I-CAR/ASE DRP technician), so the survival lever stops at the gated formats.
poles: lean on family labor to survive
hire credentialed labor to enter a gated lane
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use family labor to clear thin margins in ungated lanes but budget credentialed hires for smog and DRP collision

conflict_axes.name: product_resale_vs_service_attach
conflict_axes.description: Standalone tire and parts product resale loses to chains and online on margin, while attached service carries the model; the product line versus the labor line trade.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat product resale as a loss leader and attach alignment/brake/mechanical (tires) or trade accounts (parts) for margin

conflict_axes.name: star_test_and_repair_vs_test_only
conflict_axes.description: STAR test-and-repair captures fail-then-repair revenue and more tooling while test-only is the leanest capex; the value-capture versus lean-capex trade.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: choose test-only for the leanest entry unless repair-side volume and tooling justify test-and-repair

conflict_axes.name: jit_service_capital_vs_inventory_carry
conflict_axes.description: JIT service shops tie up capital in equipment and labor and order parts per job, while the parts retailer ties up capital in shelf inventory; the two opposite capital models behind the single parts store.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: do not enter inventory-carry parts against the nationals without a wholesale/trade base; prefer the JIT service capital model locally

conflict_axes.name: essential_demand_resilience_vs_ev_erosion
conflict_axes.description: The aging ag/fleet parc keeps essential service dense today while EV adoption (smog-exempt BEVs, no multi-speed transmission) slowly erodes the smog and transmission pools; today's resilience versus the long-run headwind.
poles: discount for the EV erosion headwind
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the resilient essential lanes but model the EV erosion into smog and transmission long-run viability and favor EV-readiness as white space

edge_cases.description: A new body shop is budgeted on accident demand and booth capex but cannot land insurer DRP relationships
edge_cases.trigger: a collision concept treats accident volume, not DRP, as the obstacle
edge_cases.mitigation: confirm DRP relationships are attainable before financing booth/frame capex; DRP, not demand, is the binding gate

edge_cases.description: A smog station's revenue is quoted using the $30-$80 test price as a regulated fact
edge_cases.trigger: the unregulated market price is conflated with the regulated $8.25 certificate fee
edge_cases.mitigation: state only the $8.25 fee as regulated and label the $30-$80 test price a competitive market estimate

edge_cases.description: A tire shop is run on standalone tire resale without service attach
edge_cases.trigger: a tire-only model competes on tire price against chains and online
edge_cases.mitigation: attach alignment, brake and mechanical service; treat tire resale as a loss leader not the margin source

edge_cases.description: A second independent parts store enters a lane the nationals own
edge_cases.trigger: an inventory-carry parts concept is planned without a wholesale/trade base
edge_cases.mitigation: do not enter inventory-carry parts retail against AutoZone/O'Reilly/NAPA and online without a trade-account base

edge_cases.description: A transmission or smog pro forma ignores the EV erosion of its demand pool
edge_cases.trigger: a long-run plan assumes a static parc as BEVs grow
edge_cases.mitigation: model the BEV-exemption and no-multi-speed-transmission erosion into long-run viability and watch the local EV ramp

edge_cases.description: A named business's revenue is requested or asserted as an actual figure
edge_cases.trigger: a question demands the real sales of a specific Turlock shop
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse to state actual revenue; provide only a labeled benchmark estimate with confidence and a confirmation path

edge_cases.description: A sector aggregate is divided by 19 and reported as a typical auto business
edge_cases.trigger: someone divides a parc-times-spend total by the 19 catalog count
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse the divide-by-19; lead with per-sub-category bands across the ~30x range and label any aggregate low confidence

edge_cases.description: A supplier-to-named-business link is upgraded from inference to a stated contract
edge_cases.trigger: an answer asserts a specific shop buys from a named distributor without a source
edge_cases.mitigation: keep supplier-to-business links labeled representative inference unless a cited source states the relationship

edge_cases.description: Functional mechanical-repair capacity is undercounted by reading only primary categories
edge_cases.trigger: a saturation read counts three primary mechanical shops and ignores cross-sellers
edge_cases.mitigation: count secondary categories: tire, transmission and smog-and-repair shops add functional mechanical capacity beyond the headline three

edge_cases.description: The cataloged 2.6/10k density floor is treated as the true total service density
edge_cases.trigger: a saturation read uses the independents-only floor as the all-in figure
edge_cases.mitigation: report 2.6/10k as a floor and the ~6-10/10k all-in (chains, dealers, informal tail) as the true density

edge_cases.description: A licensed-inspector or I-CAR/ASE technician shortage blocks a gated-format entry family labor cannot fill
edge_cases.trigger: a smog or DRP collision plan assumes family labor clears the credential
edge_cases.mitigation: budget credentialed hires for the gated lanes; family labor cannot substitute for a licensed inspector or DRP technician

workflow.action: Size the resident parc and ag/fleet demand floor
workflow.description: State the population, household, registered-vehicle parc and ag/fleet figures as cited facts or labeled estimates
workflow.gate: population, household count and the registered-vehicle parc estimate with range and confidence are stated and the ag/fleet feature named

workflow.action: Map community channels to the formats they sustain
workflow.description: Tie each ancestry share to its referral channel and fleet demand and the informal tail
workflow.gate: the Hispanic, Assyrian, Portuguese/Azorean and Punjabi shares have cited figures and named channels

workflow.action: Apply the chain crowd-out and Modesto ceiling
workflow.description: Identify which lanes chains own and which high-ticket work leaks to Modesto
workflow.gate: the chain-owned commodity lanes and Modesto's size/distance are stated and formats ranked by exposure

workflow.description: State gross/labor/parts/net benchmarks by sub-category and the $8.25-vs-market-price distinction with sources
workflow.gate: gross, labor, parts and net ranges are stated as cited planning priors and the regulated fee is distinguished from the market price

workflow.description: Define benchmark-times-size-signal banding with the estimate label, the ~30x range and the confirmation path
workflow.gate: every band carries the estimate-not-actual label, a confidence, a size signal and a confirmation source, and the ~30x range is stated

workflow.action: Identify the family-labor, supply and service-attach levers
workflow.description: Explain how family labor, the supplier map and service attach move the margin
workflow.gate: the family-labor labor-share suppression, its credential-bottleneck limit, and the service-attach mechanism are stated

workflow.action: Map suppliers and the capex ladder per sub-category
workflow.description: Name the paint/parts, jobber, tire, transmission and buying-group nodes and the JIT-vs-inventory capital split as inference
workflow.gate: each major sub-category has named supplier nodes with the inference label and the capex ladder is ranked

workflow.action: Establish the BAR, STAR and DRP licensing gates
workflow.description: State the BAR ARD floor, the STAR/smog fork and the DRP/collision gate with sources
workflow.gate: the mandatory BAR ARD floor and the STAR and DRP gates are stated with sources

workflow.action: Model each sub-category's unit economics including the gate-heavy formats
workflow.description: For each sub-category state operations, cost center, labor, benchmark band and saturation tie, tying collision to the DRP/capex gate, smog to the analyzer/STAR fork and $8.25/test-price honesty, and transmission to the high-ARO specialty
workflow.gate: each sub-category names its cost center, labeled band and the gate or lever that decides viability, and the DRP gate, the smog fee honesty and the high-gross-thin-net caveat are stated

workflow.action: Synthesize the per-sub-category saturation and white space
workflow.description: Give the crowded/adequate/thin read, the floor-vs-all-in density and rank the white space
workflow.gate: each sub-category has a saturation read, the density floor is stated and the white space is ranked

workflow.action: Issue the merged format go/no-go verdict
workflow.description: Intersect demand headroom, licensing gate and margin reality into an add/avoid call
workflow.gate: the verdict states the saturation read, binding licensing/capex gate and margin reality and is conditioned on clearing the BAR/STAR/DRP gate and attaching service

priority_rationale: The parc demand floor, community channels and the chain/Modesto ceiling come first because every format judgment depends on knowing the size and shape of vehicle demand; the cost-structure backbone, labeled-revenue method, family-labor and service-attach levers, supplier map and capex ladder next, because they are the lenses that turn the parc into unit economics; the BAR ARD, STAR and DRP gates next, because they decide enterability independent of demand; the seven sub-category models then apply all of that to concrete businesses; and the saturation synthesis and merged go/no-go come last because they compose every upstream output into a defensible add/avoid verdict, with the binding honesty rule that no per-business dollar figure is ever stated as fact.

dominance_rules.rule: The honesty label dominates any revenue claim
dominance_rules.rationale: no per-business revenue is public, so a band may never be presented as an actual figure
dominance_rules.trigger: any dollar figure is attached to a named business or sub-category
dominance_rules.action: tag it estimate-not-actual with a confidence and confirmation path, and refuse an actual-revenue claim

dominance_rules.rule: The licensing gate dominates demand headroom in any entry verdict
dominance_rules.rationale: a demand-true white space that cannot clear BAR ARD, STAR or DRP and capex is not enterable
dominance_rules.trigger: a go recommendation rests on demand alone
dominance_rules.action: withhold the go until the binding licensing/capex gate is shown clearable

dominance_rules.rule: Net margin dominates gross revenue in judging attractiveness
dominance_rules.rationale: high-gross formats still net only single digits, so revenue must not be read as profit
dominance_rules.trigger: a format is judged by its revenue band alone
dominance_rules.action: pair the band with its gross/labor/parts/net benchmark before deciding

dominance_rules.rule: The DRP gate dominates the collision-entry decision
dominance_rules.rationale: landing insurer DRP relationships, not finding accident volume, decides collision viability
dominance_rules.trigger: a collision concept is scoped on accident demand without confirming DRP
dominance_rules.action: confirm DRP relationships are attainable or do not enter

dominance_rules.rule: Service attach dominates product resale in commodity lanes
dominance_rules.rationale: standalone tire and parts resale loses to chains and online on margin
dominance_rules.trigger: a tire or parts concept is planned on product margin alone
dominance_rules.action: require attached service or a wholesale/trade base before treating the lane as viable

dominance_rules.rule: The regulated $8.25 fee dominates the $30-$80 market price in any smog fact claim
dominance_rules.rationale: only the certificate fee is regulated; the test price is a competitive estimate
dominance_rules.trigger: a smog price is stated as a regulated fact
dominance_rules.action: state the $8.25 fee as regulated and label the test price an estimate

dominance_rules.rule: Per-sub-category bands dominate any sector aggregate for the typical business
dominance_rules.rationale: the seven sub-categories span a ~30x per-firm range so no aggregate is a typical figure
dominance_rules.trigger: a sector total is divided by 19 and cited as typical
dominance_rules.action: lead with the per-sub-category bands and label any aggregate low confidence

dominance_rules.rule: Documented relationships dominate inferred supplier links
dominance_rules.rationale: supplier-to-business links are representative inference unless a cited source states the relationship
dominance_rules.action: label it inference unless a cited source confirms it

dominance_rules.rule: The credential bottleneck dominates family labor in gated lanes
dominance_rules.rationale: family labor cannot clear a licensed-inspector or I-CAR/ASE requirement
dominance_rules.trigger: a smog or DRP collision plan assumes family labor fills a credentialed role
dominance_rules.action: budget credentialed hires for the gated lanes

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach the estimate-not-actual label when the band is first produced, not after review
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a revenue figure circulating as a fact and having to be retracted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm DRP relationships are attainable before financing booth/frame capex
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a launched collision shop stalling because insurer DRP volume never materializes

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pair every revenue band with its net benchmark in the same step
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a high-gross format being approved before the thin DRP-compressed net is seen

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run a white space through the licensing and service-attach gate before calling it an opportunity
anti_rework_rules.prevents: recommending a demand-true but gate-blocked or resale-only format and reversing the call

anti_rework_rules.rule: State the $8.25 fee as the only regulated smog figure from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: the $30-$80 test price hardening into an asserted regulated fact that must be corrected

anti_rework_rules.rule: Distinguish a sector aggregate from a per-sub-category band before quoting any per-firm figure
anti_rework_rules.prevents: anchoring stakeholders on a typical-business number that no firm across a 30x range earns

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep supplier-to-business links labeled inference from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an inferred supply link hardening into an asserted contract that must later be corrected

anti_rework_rules.rule: Count secondary categories when reading mechanical capacity from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an undercount of functional mechanical capacity that misreads saturation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Budget credentialed hires for smog and DRP collision before assuming family labor clears them
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a gated-format plan stalling on a credential family labor cannot fill

iteration_protocol.trigger: CDTFA seller's-permit or BAR station data becomes available
iteration_protocol.action: replace the labeled revenue bands and density reads with confirmed figures and re-rank confidence

iteration_protocol.trigger: a Census ACS or DMV registration refresh changes population, income, parc or ancestry shares
iteration_protocol.action: re-size the parc floor and re-map the community channels and saturation reads

iteration_protocol.trigger: a parts/paint/tire/kit supplier consolidation or a buying-group change lands
iteration_protocol.action: update the affected sub-category cost centers and the supply-chain and capex nodes

iteration_protocol.trigger: a BAR/STAR fee or program rule or the DRP standard changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-evaluate the gated-format entry gates and the collision and smog verdicts

iteration_protocol.trigger: a shop opens or closes, changing a per-sub-category count
iteration_protocol.action: update the saturation read and the merged go/no-go for that sub-category

iteration_protocol.trigger: the local EV share of the parc grows materially
iteration_protocol.action: update the smog and transmission erosion reads and re-rank the EV-readiness white space

iteration_protocol.trigger: a cross-shop leakage study or measured Modesto-capture figure is produced
iteration_protocol.action: replace the behavioral leakage estimate and re-rank the gate-capped formats

iteration_protocol.trigger: a labor-rate, parts-cost or commodity (tire, paint, transmission-kit) price swing lands
iteration_protocol.action: update the cost backbone and the affected format cost centers

required_checks: all edge ids unique EDGE_XXX format
all from/to in edges reference valid node ids
all competency_question_refs resolve to valid CQ ids
all evidence_refs resolve to valid source_registry ids
all priority_order entries are valid node ids with no duplicates
high_risk_nodes (risk_if_wrong>=0.80) have non-empty acceptance_tests and human_review_required=true
conflict edges have signed_tension<0 and resolution_rule present
observed_impact=0.0 for all nodes (no observed data)
19-24 nodes, 32-40 edges, 8-10 conflict_axes, 10-12 edge_cases, 9-12 workflow steps
post_formula_checks: all derived fields non-zero after compute run
